_note: The farm monitor's design record: the artefacts chapters 1-9 handed over, in one file, in the form `design.py dossier` prints. Tables that an earlier chapter's tool produces (never-list, placement, growth, link selection, inventory, bill) are not copied here; the dossier runs those tools on their own JSON. What is here is what no earlier tool prints: the quality numbers, the stream and task tables as decided, the farm monitor's own safety layers (chapter 5's example was the incubator), the fleet and rollout parameters, and the hand-over checklist with the file that holds each artefact.
name: farm monitor

nodes.link: Wi-Fi, HTTPS on a kept TLS session + SSE on settings/desired
LoRaWAN class A, SF8, 11-byte frame every 10 min
LoRaWAN to the plot node, Wi-Fi to the router
nodes.senses: nothing (translates frames into records; shares the outdoor reading by a local hop)

quality.from: N2: three missed periods is a 45 s detection delay
N3: ten misses before offline keeps false alarms rare
N6: outages are minutes, not days

quality.value: 30 days hot in the database, 2 years in a bucket
quality.from: brief B3 (a week) and chapter 8's storage line

streams.fields: schema dev ts t h soil tank fan valve rssi fw seq up_s rst boots heap_min

streams.kept: 30 d in the database, 2 y in the bucket

streams.mode: overwrite, version echoed, clamped on the device
overwrite; manifest URL and version / download, flashing, pending, valid, rolled back

tasks.writes: fan, valve, fault; pulses the gate; the only caller of the interlock

safe_states.why: a fan running for no reason costs electricity; a greenhouse without one overheats
a valve open for no reason floods a plot and empties the tank

layers.senses: the sensor; the tank level trend
layers.catches: what the firmware can see: limits, max on-time 30 min, a sensor that lies by range or staleness

layers.acts_through: a reset; the pin held low

layers.senses: silence, or a fault the firmware declared (it stops pulsing)
layers.acts_through: a second relay in series with the valve
layers.catches: a hung MCU, a shorted valve relay once the firmware sees the level fall
a shorted valve relay the firmware never notices

layers.senses: the buzzer; the app's offline and fault alerts (N3)
layers.catches: power loss (both safe states hold: the fan contactor drops, the valve closes), a fan stuck off

accepted.failure: fan relay or contactor stuck off
accepted.why: not a hazard to people; the firmware sees the temperature rise with the fan commanded on, declares a fault, and the alert path raises a repair call
both actuators fall to their safe state without firmware: the contactor drops and the valve closes; only N3 remains, and the app shows the unit offline after 10 minutes

cloud.shape: A: Firebase Realtime Database, Spark plan
cloud.why: chapter 8 K1-K5 at the brief's size: $0 a month, no operator, two 'you build' rows
you_build: nightly export of history older than 30 days to a bucket
signed OTA manifest and the rollout script (chapter 9)
cloud.listeners: on /devices/<id>/status only; charts by an indexed limitToLast query on /history
cloud.identity: per-device custom token in NVS from chapter 7's claim flow; rules confine each device to its own path with shape checks
cloud.presence: status age over 10 misses per class, judged by a scheduled function; there is no last will on shape A
cloud.migration: to shape B when K1 or the bill says so: the records (chapter 3) and the comms contract (chapter 6) do not change; the transport becomes MQTT on a kept session and presence gains the last will as a faster clock

table_lines: firmware versions and the units a rollout cannot reach
reboots by reason and loop suspects
alerts: offline above 5 % of the fleet (at the brief's size: any unit)
any unit under the 20 kB heap floor

rollout.signing: Ed25519 private key on the operator's laptop; public key compiled into every image; manifest with the eight fields of chapter 9
rollout.stages: gh2 first (one unit), soak one hour while the fleet table is read per version, then gh1 and the gateway
rollout.halt: any rollback halts and withdraws the desired record (with a first stage of one unit, the halt rate is 1 over 1)
rollout.plot_node: no over-the-air update over LoRaWAN (FUOTA is out of this handbook's scope); the plot node is reflashed by cable at a site visit, so its image must be the most conservative one

handover.artefact: the never-list as JSON with the checker at zero gaps for N1-N6 (N7 closed by chapter 7)
the computation list and the decision table
the traffic table for the candidate paths
the stream table, the settings contract, the growth table, migration code and sample records
the task table, ownership table, safe states, interlock truth table, boot order, watchdog policy
the layer table, energy-path diagram, sizing sheet, one bench test per layer, the accepted rows
the link table per node, airtime and energy sheets, the comms contract
the inventory at zero gaps, the credential design, the rules file and scenarios, the claim flow, the rotation runbook
the fit table, the bill with sources, the listener rule, the rules file in the chosen dialect
the health fields, the fleet table queries, the presence rule, the manifest schema and eight checks, the rollout plan
the bill of materials, the traceability matrix, the three-year cost
